core.title: Name artifacts as theme(:category)*:aspect(.variant)?
core.given: An artifact name is being written, changed, or referenced in any document (any plan artifact, acceptance, contract, or other document — non-exhaustive).
core.when: The planner writes that artifact name or a reference to it.
core.then: Write the name as {theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})? — exactly one theme, zero or more hierarchy categories, exactly one leaf aspect, and an optional variant, every part kebab-case.
prefer: Start with the top-level architectural theme as the namespace (kebab-case ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$).
Use colons only for hierarchy (vertical depth): each category navigates one level down the resource tree; depth is unlimited.
End the colon path with the leaf resource noun as the aspect.
Use a single dot only for a variant: a lateral variation, facet, or state of the aspect (typically at most one).
Use the simple form theme:aspect when no hierarchy is needed.
avoid: Omitting the theme or the aspect, or naming with more than one theme or aspect.
Using a dot for hierarchy or a colon for a variant.
Non-kebab-case parts (uppercase, underscores, leading digits or hyphens).
core.why: Theme-based namespacing gives semantic clarity and collision-free names, colons give unlimited hierarchical depth and dots lateral variants, and the structure keeps artifact names aligned with contract file paths.
evidence: Every written, changed, or referenced artifact name matches ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)*:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)?$ (theme, categories, aspect, optional variant).
Reviewer confirms colon segments express hierarchy and any dot segment is a lateral variant of the aspect, not a deeper level.
verification: Grammar check: every written, changed, or referenced artifact name must match {theme}(:{category})*:{aspect}(.{variant})? — colons express vertical hierarchy, the single dot a lateral variant, the theme is the namespace; every part kebab-case.
Scope: check artifact names wherever they appear (any document type), including references to existing artifacts, not only newly created names.

Detecting names that are written, changed, or newly referenced requires a diff-level observer that extracts artifact-name strings from any edited document and reports names added, changed, or newly referenced.

Semantic fit — that colon segments express hierarchy and any dot segment is a lateral variant of the aspect rather than a deeper level — is reviewer-confirmed; the mechanical check covers name structure only.

values: artifact name written, changed, or referenced

fires: Planner writes an artifact name — creating, renaming, or referencing/using an existing artifact by name — in any document type.
Planner adds a new artifact to a wagon's produce or consume list and must name it.
Planner renames an existing artifact or introduces a variant of an existing aspect.
Planner writes or changes a reference to an existing artifact by name in a plan artifact, acceptance, contract, or any other document.
Planner names an artifact in a contract (e.g. its identifier or URN) with no plan or wagon change.
doesNotFire: Planner edits prose in any document without writing, changing, or referencing any artifact name.
Naming of wagons themselves (covered by the wagon URN naming convention, which only shares the kebab grammar).
Code-level identifiers (functions, variables, files) that are not artifact names.

neutralityNotes: The convention is a naming grammar and is inherently stack-neutral, so the core is essentially the Bun obligation verbatim and needs nothing from a structure profile; profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty, and no vocabulary key was stretched to fit. 'Wagon', 'plan', 'URN' and 'contract' are kept as cross-stack ATDD planning vocabulary (the stack-neutral profile vocabulary itself defines wagons and URNs, e.g. layout.wagon_dir, urn.wagon), not as stack names. The realization's concrete document-kind examples (plans, wagons, WMBTs, acceptances, contracts, docs) and concrete valid-name examples (commons:ux:foundations:color, orders:checkout, ...) stay in bun.json, which is delivered as the worked reference example; because the Bun scope is explicitly 'any document, non-exhaustive', replacing the example lists with the unbounded role-level scope neither weakens nor strengthens the obligation. bun.json declares no severity or disposition, so core verification records none; it also names no detector/validator/finding ids (only the term id name_component, classified bunOnly).
